questions.q: Did the aggregation logic inside gold.daily_sales_summary need to change because of the Silver-layer redesign?
options: No — it still just groups silver.sales_clean by store_id and sale_date and aggregates, exactly as before
Yes — it now needs its own MERGE INTO statement
Yes — it now needs to read directly from bronze.sales_raw instead of Silver
Yes — it now needs to group by transaction_id instead of store_id and sale_date
questions.explain: The aggregation logic is unchanged: group by store_id and sale_date, sum total_amount, count transaction_id. Only what feeds Silver changed, not how Gold reads it.

questions.q: What does gold.daily_sales_summary's aggregation sum and count, respectively?
options: Sums total_amount into total_sales; counts transaction_id into total_transactions
Sums quantity into total_sales; counts category into total_transactions
Sums transaction_id into total_sales; counts store_id into total_transactions
Counts total_amount into total_sales; sums transaction_id into total_transactions
questions.explain: The table's fixed schema sums total_amount into total_sales and counts transaction_id values into total_transactions, grouped by store_id and sale_date.

questions.q: Why didn't the Bronze-to-Silver redesign require any changes to gold.daily_sales_summary?
options: Because this Gold table only depends on Silver's current contents, not on the process that produced those contents — the medallion pattern decouples the two
Because gold.daily_sales_summary doesn't actually read from silver.sales_clean
Because the redesign only affected gold.category_breakdown, not silver.sales_clean
Because Delta Lake tables cannot have their upstream maintenance strategy changed
questions.explain: Each layer in the medallion pattern depends on the contents of the layer below it, not on how that layer is maintained — that decoupling is why Gold needed no changes.

questions.q: According to this lesson, are gold.daily_sales_summary's totals now more or less trustworthy than before the redesign?
options: More trustworthy — because Silver itself is now more trustworthy, correctly handling late-arriving data instead of relying on luck
Less trustworthy — the incremental MERGE introduces more risk of error
Exactly the same, because nothing about Silver's correctness changed
It's impossible to tell without re-running the Beginner project's pipeline
questions.explain: Because Silver now correctly attributes late-arriving sales to their real sale_date via the transaction_id-keyed MERGE, Gold's totals built on top of it are more reliable than before.

questions.q: What is the core engineering principle this lesson lands on?
options: Gold logic is decoupled from how Silver got populated, as long as Silver's end state is correct
Every Gold table must be rebuilt with MERGE INTO whenever Silver changes
Bronze, Silver, and Gold must always use identical write modes
A table's aggregation logic should be rewritten every time its source table's row count changes
questions.explain: This is the chapter's central takeaway: well-layered design lets you change how a layer is maintained without rippling changes into layers built on top of it, as long as that layer's final contents are correct.
